analysis.title: "The Weakest Borrowers Are Telling A Different Story": Morgan Stanley On Record CCC Stress And Oversold Banks
key_insights: Headline indices and the underlying market diverge. The S&P 500 is near record highs and MSCI World is up 13.5% YTD, but the Russell 2000 has fallen five straight weeks and 54% of Russell 3000 stocks have had drawdowns above 20% since June.

MS QDS data: two-week realized vol on the S&P 500 is at the 14th percentile of the past five years and weighted single-name vol at the 40th. Two-week S&P dispersion is at the 79th percentile and between-sector to within-sector dispersion is at the 28th, so the action is stock-by-stock.

Mike Wilson notes the S&P forward P/E is back near 19x and the de-rating beneath the surface is advancing while earnings stay strong. Global P/E multiples contracted 8% in 3Q, the largest de-rating in a rising market since 1994.
Wilson's favorite risk/reward is Industrials, where Capital Goods revisions breadth has climbed to 38%. His screen includes CAT, GD, ITW and EME, and his Fresh Money Buy List adds TGT, NOC and AMT.

Consensus expects 29.5% YoY S&P 500 EPS growth in 3Q, with the Mag7 contributing roughly a quarter. 37.3% of S&P market cap reports the week of October 26. Earnings growth is narrow: Micron and Nvidia deliver about a third of it, and a Goldman partner found 10 stocks drive 68%.

In MS's 2Q data, stocks with rising 2026 EPS and rising FCF estimates gained a median 1.7% the day after reporting, while those with rising EPS but falling FCF lost 0.8%. Wilson expects earnings quality, FCF and revisions breadth to drive the same split in 3Q.

Early reporters: PEP beat a low bar but cut guidance, STZ beat with weak beer demand and margins, LEVI raised its outlook despite softer revenue, and DAL reported September-quarter revenue up about 16%. Single-name implied vol is elevated in Industrials and Financials, so the market is expected to be less forgiving of misses.

US banks have fallen 13% since August and their 14-day RSI is 27, while the S&P 500 RSI is above 60 with the index 0.2% from its all-time high. The 33-point gap is the widest since 1993. BKX forward P/E is below its 10Y median of about 11.9x.

Manan Gosalia expects a fairly neutral 3Q for large cap banks, with capital markets activity moderating ahead of the midterms. He expects 14% median EPS growth in 2027 and 13% in 2028, with large caps at about 10x forward earnings. His preferred names into Tuesday's prints are STT, C, BAC and FITB, and he upgraded WFC to Overweight and Top Pick with a $102 PT.

Financials are 10.9% of hedge funds' North American net exposure per MS Prime Brokerage. That is the 100th percentile of the past year but the 13th percentile since 2010. Funds added banks this year from a low base, so recent adds are underwater.
Alvaro Serrano is more relaxed on European banks, saying it would take a prolonged period of bond market volatility and OAT-Bund spread widening to derail them.

US HY spreads are at the 16th percentile since 1994, but CCC spreads have closed above 1,000bp, the widest since 2023 and the 77th percentile. The CCC to broader HY spread ratio is at a record high. MS says this divergence has historically peaked ahead of a worse credit cycle, though similar CCC levels in 1998, 2011, 2015 and 2022 did not immediately signal recession.
Savone ties credit stress to higher rates and refinancing costs. Heavy debt issuance from Broadcom, Oracle and SpaceX at 6%+ all-in yields could crowd out weaker borrowers.

MS's European derivatives desk is pitching protection on its weak balance sheet basket (MSSTWKBS, about 50% Real Estate, leveraged Industrials and indebted Telcos). The basket fell 20% in the 2022 rate shock and its realized vol is below the SX5E's, so the hedge is cheap.

US Treasury yields reached 5.30% this week, the highest since 2002, and EUR/USD fell to 1.12, a 17-month low. The 10Y is at the 100th percentile of its ten-year range. A 30Y auction on Thursday priced at the highest yield since August 2000.

Michael Gapen sees policy as neutral to modestly restrictive. His real neutral rate estimate has risen from under 100bp to about 150bp since early 2025 and financial conditions have tightened 100bp since February. He keeps two more 25bp hikes in December and March, taking fed funds to 4.25-4.50%, despite 29K September payrolls.
Gapen expects Wednesday's CPI at 0.24% MoM core (from 0.29%) and 0.62% headline, driven by $100+ oil. An upside core miss would put the October meeting back in play.

Jens Eisenschmidt estimates France needs a primary surplus of 2% of GDP to stabilize its debt, a EUR150B fiscal adjustment, and sees French debt near 160% of GDP by 2040. A France-Germany 10Y spread above 200bp is a potential TPI threshold, with spreads now near 140bp.
Takeshi Yamaguchi notes Japan pays more than $25/bbl over Dubai futures for physical crude because of tanker freight, and sees Japan core CPI topping 3% as energy subsidies expire.

Hedge funds were the largest net sellers of US equities since July, concentrated in AI infrastructure (semis, optical networking, agentic AI beneficiaries), biotech and AI health care, and bought staples, utilities and real estate. US L/S gross leverage is 207% (91st percentile since 2010) against net of 52%. Americas L/S funds are down 0.4% MTD versus +1.5% for the S&P.

Stephen Byrd's team estimates a 34% net US power shortfall through 2028, with hyperscaler capacity additions rising from 11.0GW in 2025 to 32.2GW in 2027 and 39.0GW in 2028. MS expects rising premia for time-to-power solutions such as behind-the-meter generation and repurposed bitcoin-mining grid access.

Percoco and Arcaro argue a growing power shortfall, inference moving to smaller nodes and political resistance to mega-campus data centers point to a structural shift toward distributed behind-the-meter power. Percoco upgraded BWA on its turbine generator.

An MS AlphaWise survey shows AI at 45% favorable vs 31% unfavorable. Net sentiment toward a data center within about 10 miles of home is -20%, and opposition to a nearby facility rose to 41% from 25%.

MS derivatives calls gold a top commodity pick on the pullback. Central banks bought 289t in 2Q26, an annualized pace of about 1,155t versus 860t in 2025, and gold trades materially stronger than its link to real yields implies.
Erik Woodring sees PC units down 14% in 2026 and 11% in 2027, seven points below consensus, with HPQ ($19 PT, 41% downside) a top Underweight.
Brian Nowak sees Waymo reaching about 1.1 billion annual trips and about $21B of revenue by 2032.

MS's cross-asset Market Sentiment Indicator flipped positive, exiting the risk-off reading held since July 21. The regime has been associated with above-average one-week forward returns for global equities.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings growth of 29.5% expected for 3Q and rising estimates, with the S&P near record highs and a positive sentiment indicator, could lift stocks priced for good results.
tension_points.bear_case: CCC spreads above 1,000bp and a record CCC to HY ratio have historically peaked ahead of a worse credit cycle, with Treasury yields at 5.30% and banks oversold.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Disappointing bank earnings Tuesday or an upside core CPI miss Wednesday that revives an October hike.

tension_points.bear_case: Rates, oil and AI disruption fears weigh on banks, and recent hedge fund adds are underwater.
